clue.text: Beatles, before Beatles prey on people

parts.note: a hunted animal is the hunter's quarry
men is a common crossword word for people in general

explanation.surface: A rock fan complains that the Beatles are predators feeding on the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just joins the two pieces. The Quarrymen were John Lennon's skiffle group, the band that became the Beatles.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the name of the Liverpool skiffle group from which the Beatles grew, so it is the Beatles at an earlier stage.

clue.text: Game birds cower

definitions.meaning: small plump birds shot for sport, the plural the same as the singular

explanation.definitionFit: The noun names small partridge-like game birds; the verb means to flinch or recoil in fear, as a coward cowers.

clue.text: Elia sang off key -just what the doctor ordered?

indicators.note: a singer who is off key is out of tune, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: C is a musical key

explanation.surface: Charles Lamb's alter ego Elia sings out of tune, and someone finds it soothing medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges ELIA SANG into ANALGESI; 'key' then supplies C. Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: A painkiller is a typical medicine a doctor prescribes, and the question mark admits the definition is playful.

clue.text: Posh car commonly taken to a dance or a movie

parts.note: Roller is the informal British name for a Rolls-Royce
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone arrives at a dance, or at the cinema, in a Rolls-Royce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken to' only joins the car to the dance. Rollerball is a 1975 film starring James Caan.
explanation.definitionFit: Rollerball is a 1975 science-fiction film about a violent future sport, so it is a specific film title.

clue.text: Derision for male lacking right garden feature

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is missing from the next word's synonym

parts.note: a rockery is a bed of stones and alpine plants in a garden

explanation.surface: Gardeners sneer at a man whose plot lacks a proper feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garden feature' reads as the subject of the surface; it is only the source word that loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Mockery is ridicule or scorn, the same contemptuous treatment as derision.

clue.text: Savings invested in Shell?

parts.note: reads as money put into shares of the oil company Shell, but means a reserve of money pictured as something sitting inside a shell

explanation.walkthrough: The capital S makes Shell look like the oil company; the clue really pictures something laid in a bird's nest inside its shell.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means money saved up for the future, likened to an egg left in a nest to encourage hens to lay.

clue.text: Female left by Jack Ruby, say?

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: Jack Ruby, the man who shot Lee Harvey Oswald, leaves a woman behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Ruby shot Kennedy's assassin, but here the two words split: Jack is J and Ruby is the definition. 'by' simply places EWE and L beside J.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruby is a precious stone, one example of a gem, signalled by 'say'.

clue.text: Scots beloved by the Spanish prophet

parts.note: jo is a Scots word for a sweetheart, as in Burns's John Anderson, my jo
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Scottish sweetheart is adored by the people of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Joel is one of the minor prophets of the Hebrew Bible, with a book named after him.

clue.text: Innocent Selborne naturalist

definitions.meaning: Gilbert ... wrote The Natural History of Selborne, a Hampshire village

explanation.definitionFit: The colour stands for purity and blamelessness; Gilbert White was the eighteenth-century parson-naturalist who chronicled wildlife in Selborne.

clue.text: He tingled all over, having lost weight

indicators.note: all over suggests the letters are scattered everywhere, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man felt tingles through his whole body after a successful diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over' looks like part of the tingling, but it rearranges HE TINGLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Made less heavy is the literal sense, so a load relieved of weight has been made lighter.

clue.text: Benefit from a disguise, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says what we hear when the words are spoken

parts.note: a gives A; a veil hides the face, a form of disguise

explanation.surface: Someone profits from going about in disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link. 'reportedly' says A VEIL is heard, which gives the letters of a verb meaning to help.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to be of use or advantage, as in 'of no avail'.

clue.text: Pampering insects, go to pot

indicators.note: go to pot means fall into ruin, so the letters of the words before are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spoils the garden bugs while their plants run to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go to pot' reads as one idiom, but 'go' is part of the fodder and 'to pot' alone signals the rearrangement of INSECTS GO.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosset is to coddle or spoil someone with excessive care, so cosseting is indulging them.

clue.text: Number called for supporters by team

parts.note: legs support a body or a table
a football or cricket team is an eleven

explanation.surface: Fans of a team are summoned by name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'by' only join. In bingo, a caller announces numbers with nicknames, and 11 is 'legs eleven' because the figures look like two legs.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the traditional British bingo caller's nickname for the number 11.

clue.text: Some redundant, extraneous words

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An editor complains that some of the wording is superfluous.
explanation.definitionFit: Written matter, the body of words in a document or book, is its text.

clue.text: Lead, say, in a sort of band

definitions.meaning: lead is an example of a dense metallic element
a loud rock music genre, and the groups that play it

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' just joins the two definitions. Lead is the metal, not the singer up front.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is a typical dense metal element, and the same phrase names a loud, guitar-heavy genre of rock.

clue.text: Plant by sea or at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and lost, so the letters before are muddled

explanation.surface: A coastal plant grows by the shore or out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges BY SEA OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosebay willowherb is a tall pink-flowered weed, a familiar wild plant.

clue.text: Do they fix things for theatrical high-fliers?

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
airmen fly high in aircraft

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether these workers do jobs for trapeze artists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' joins. 'high-fliers' suggests acrobats or achievers, but means pilots.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradesmen who mend broken things are menders by profession.

clue.text: Troublemaker getting girl involved with men

indicators.note: involved means tangled together, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A mischief-maker sets a young woman up with several men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' and 'with' only join; 'involved' mixes GIRL with MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary mischievous sprite blamed for mechanical faults, so a source of trouble.

clue.text: Academic entertained by individualists — they're all capital people

indicators.note: being entertained by someone puts a guest inside their home

parts.note: loners keep to themselves, going their own way
a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A professor is hosted by solitary types, all of them city folk.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a university teacher, chiefly at Oxford or Cambridge. 'capital' is the definition's pun on London, the capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhabitants of Britain's capital city are called by this name, so they are capital people.

clue.text: Cream was first drunk

parts.note: the pick of the bunch is its best, the cream
led means was in front, ahead of the rest

explanation.surface: Someone recalls that the dairy cream got eaten before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickled is informal slang for intoxicated, as if preserved in alcohol.

clue.text: Graduates caught in the act may be sent down

indicators.note: something caught in another thing is held inside it

parts.note: a deed is an act
BA is a Bachelor of Arts, so BAS are graduates

explanation.surface: Students caught red-handed may be expelled from university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' is a link. 'sent down' sounds like expulsion from university, which suits the graduates, but here it means lowered.
explanation.definitionFit: To debase is to lower in quality or value, so debased means brought down.

clue.text: Kicked the bucket full of wine, as foretold

indicators.note: a container full of something holds it inside

parts.note: kicked the bucket is slang for died
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: A drunk dies after tipping over a pail brimming with wine, as predicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link. 'Kicked the bucket' is English slang for died, and the surface's literal bucket of wine is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to discover by intuition or supernatural insight, as a prophet predicts.

clue.text: Old cars taken from compound at sunset

indicators.note: taken from says the letters are lifted out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Vintage vehicles are driven out of a walled enclosure as the sun goes down.
explanation.walkthrough: Datsun was the old name of the Japanese car brand now sold as Nissan.
explanation.definitionFit: Datsun is a former Japanese car marque, so its models are cars of a bygone brand.

clue.text: News of Ulster setback

indicators.note: a setback sends things backwards, so the two words are read from the end

parts.note: NI stands for Northern Ireland, often called Ulster

explanation.surface: A report from Northern Ireland tells of a reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' turns the whole run of 'of Ulster' around, not just the province. Ulster is commonly used for Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a short informal word for information, such as the latest updates.

clue.text: Tail-end missing in aviation contest

indicators.note: missing says a letter is gone from the word for aviation

parts.note: flight is the act or business of flying

indicators.note: end, fixed to Tail by a hyphen, picks the final letter of that word

explanation.surface: In an air display, a plane loses its tail section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tail-end' looks like part of a plane, but 'end' takes L from 'Tail', and 'missing' removes that L from FLIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight is a struggle or bout between opponents, the same thing as a contest.

clue.text: Cook I mess about, not eating or drinking much

indicators.note: to cook figures is to fiddle them, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef admits to fussing in the kitchen while hardly eating anything themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the person in the kitchen, but it rearranges I MESS ABOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstemious describes someone sparing and moderate in food and alcohol.

clue.text: Bear in the witness-box

definitions.meaning: to bear is to tolerate or put up with
in American courts the witness-box is called by this name

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' just joins. In a US court a witness 'takes the stand'.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up with something is to tolerate it; the stand is where a witness gives evidence in court.

clue.text: Tags on sound tool

indicators.note: sound says the letters given are those that would be heard spoken

parts.note: to tag on is to attach or append, so tags on means adds

explanation.surface: Labels are attached to a sound piece of equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'in good condition' describing the tool, but signals that ADDS is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a woodworking implement with an arched blade set at right angles to the handle.

clue.text: Cat on gold plate in African port

parts.note: mog is British slang for a cat

indicators.note: in says the plate goes inside the gold

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a dish is a plate

explanation.surface: A cat sits on a golden plate in a port in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just joins the cat to the rest. Mogadishu is the capital of Somalia, on the Indian Ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Mogadishu is the capital of Somalia and a harbour on the Indian Ocean.

clue.text: A letter is all the thanks you get!

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a note was their only reward for helping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is all' and 'you get' only join. Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, written as a circle with a bar.

clue.text: Salt intermingled?

parts.note: read as two parts, INTER and mingled: the letters of the word for salt, when mixed, make INTER, the first part of this clue word

explanation.surface: A cook asks whether the salt has been mixed in.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: split 'intermingled' into INTER plus 'mingled', and the salt's letters mingled give INTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is a chemical salt.

clue.text: Land's End is impassable, it's revealed

indicators.note: End says to take the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: a closed road cannot be passed

explanation.surface: It is announced that the road at Land's End in Cornwall is shut.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the westernmost tip of Cornwall, but here 'End' takes D from 'Land's'. 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose is to make known, so something disclosed has been made public.
